Features related to provincially tracked species and species at risk are not available as open data. Sensitive features are subject to licensing and approvals. Visit the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry website to get access to natural heritage information. 

Some species occur regularly in large multiple-species aggregations at particular locations during periods in their life cycle. Such locations are important to the conservation of the species and are referred to as a Wildlife Concentration Area (WCA). Examples of wildlife concentration areas include shorebird migratory concentration areas, raptor winter concentration areas, and bat hibernacula. 
 
A Wildlife Concentration Area Occurrence is an area with suitable habitat where a provincially tracked WCA is found. The methodology used to derive an occurrence varies by WCA type and is based on international standards developed by NatureServe that enable cross-jurisdictional comparisons of WCA occurrences. In Ontario, this methodology is coordinated by the Natural Heritage Information Centre (NHIC) of the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources. 
 
Each derived occurrence represents a summary of WCA observations.
